abstract: Optically injected semiconductor lasers are forced nonlinear oscillators whose locking boundaries are organized by codimension-two points. We ask which property of the carrier balance permits or forbids a Bogdanov--Takens (BT) point in the standard three-dimensional rate equations. Taking the carrier inversion $n$ as distinguished observable, the rate that enters the spectral conditions is the slope of the gain--loss balance, $ξ=\partial\dot n/\partial n=-2Γ/κ$, where $Γ$ is the damping of the relaxation oscillation and $κ=1+2Bn$ the normalized stimulated-emission factor. The two BT conditions become affine in $ξ$ and imply the exact sum rule $K^{2}=I[1-(1+κ)I]$ between injection amplitude $K$ and intracavity intensity $I$. The product of the two relaxation eigenvalues that survive at a saddle-node is bounded below by $1-16Γ^{2}$, so that no BT point exists for $Γ<1/4$, whatever $B$, the linewidth enhancement factor, the injection strength and the detuning; below this barrier every contact between Hopf and saddle-node curves is a fold--Hopf point. For $B=0$ the barrier is completed to an exact existence criterion. We prove that the unfolding of a BT point by injection strength and detuning is transversal if and only if two explicit curves cross transversally in the plane of locked states; for $B=0$ this is a simple root of an explicit function, and transversality fails exactly at the existence threshold. Two BT points at $Γ=1/2$, $α=2$ are verified to be generic, and the contacts between Hopf and saddle-node curves are classified into fold--Hopf, BT and nilpotent triple-zero points.
